correspondence.component_scope: opening and upper ice rock belt
correspondence.finding: The chosen northern opening is on mapped inland ice north of the coastal mountain belt. The first three stored parts proceed south into the belt of elongated exposed-rock areas and intervening ice. The supplied line overlaps rock-margin terrain as well as ice at this national map scale; this is not represented as a surveyed glacier stream or a continuous blue river. The full opening and the long third part were read, including their receiving terrain and joins.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based original stored-part numbering within the selected fragment; component scopes can overlap at joins.

correspondence.component_scope: upper to middle ice passage
correspondence.finding: The short successive parts and their joins occupy the white ice corridor south of the upper rock belt. This passage bends between elongated exposed-rock masses, with mapped ice-surface contours extending into adjacent ice passages. The original covers every intervening short part and the longer seventeenth part. The contours and connected ice terrain supply ordinary terrain correspondence, not evidence of hydraulic connectivity.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based original stored-part numbering within the selected fragment; component scopes can overlap at joins.

correspondence.component_scope: middle bends and receiving ice
correspondence.finding: These parts continue through the broader middle ice passage, east of the conspicuous red intrusive-rock patch and between exposed-rock masses. The selected bends toward the west and then south remain within the mapped ice/rock valley setting, whose neighboring ice passages and receiving corridor are visible. No selected lake, managed channel, or named river is established here.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based original stored-part numbering within the selected fragment; component scopes can overlap at joins.

correspondence.component_scope: lower narrowed ice corridor
correspondence.finding: The selection follows the lower narrowed ice passage between large exposed-rock promontories. The long twenty-second part, its turns and both joins were inspected in the clean original pixels. The mapping supports ordinary continuation through this historical glacier and coastal-mountain setting without requiring an exact present-day wet channel.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based original stored-part numbering within the selected fragment; component scopes can overlap at joins.

correspondence.component_scope: terminal approach and two endings
correspondence.finding: The final four parts approach the small coastal opening between exposed-rock promontories on Blosseville Kyst, in the vicinity of Kap Ravn. The stored source endpoint is landward/northwest of the displayed endpoint, close to the historical lower ice-tongue/coastal-opening transition. The displayed extension ends farther southeast in that same small coastal-opening setting. Both positions and the intervening selected final part were inspected separately; map scale and epoch do not support a precise contemporary ice-front, shoreline, or ordinary river-mouth claim.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based original stored-part numbering within the selected fragment; component scopes can overlap at joins.

findings.source_endpoint_description: The stored source endpoint lies landward/northwest of the render endpoint, at the historical lower ice-tongue/coastal-opening setting between exposed-rock promontories near Kap Ravn. Its exact relation to the contemporary glacier front or shore is not asserted.
findings.render_endpoint_description: The displayed ending is farther southeast within the same small coastal-opening setting on Blosseville Kyst. It is distinct from the source endpoint and is not silently substituted for it. No exact current river mouth is established.

correspondence.component_scope: chosen southern mountain opening
correspondence.finding: The selected beginning occupies a forested mountain hollow below rocky, locally snow-covered ridges. A northward enclosed drainage depression bends northeast into the same upper valley. The image shows ordinary terrain continuity; canopy prevents asserting a precise wet channel beneath every selected vertex. No separate lake transfer or intervening divide is indicated.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based original stored-part numbering, restarting within each explicitly identified fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: northeast upper valley and join
correspondence.finding: The upper route follows a narrow wooded valley northeast, makes its selected northward dogleg, and enters a larger east-northeast receiving channel. The main valley is continuous through the join. Nearby linear lakes and a separate southern side tributary are not traversed by the selected route.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based original stored-part numbering, restarting within each explicitly identified fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: middle northward turn and broadening
correspondence.finding: The selected eastern bend turns north and then northwest within a continuous channel and floodplain corridor. Forestry roads, clearings and side-water settings are visible, while the selected route remains in the main receiving valley rather than crossing to the neighboring eastern lakes. No claim about diversion operation or present flow is made.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based original stored-part numbering, restarting within each explicitly identified fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: lower valley and tributary receiving setting
correspondence.finding: The lower selection follows the widening northwest river belt past multiple meanders and open gravel/floodplain areas, receives a conspicuous valley from the southwest, and turns north into the lowland estuary approach. Adjacent side valleys are not given the mainstem name.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based original stored-part numbering, restarting within each explicitly identified fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: actual source and render coastal endings
correspondence.finding: The last stored part reaches the tidal distributary and mudflat complex. The separately preserved source endpoint is within that estuarine channel setting; the render endpoint is farther north at the connected coastal-water margin. Both are geographically covered. First-party municipal prose identifies Salmon River at Kelsey Bay, and places Kelsey Bay on Johnstone Strait. No exact present bank or tidal edge is claimed.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based original stored-part numbering, restarting within each explicitly identified fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen Pike Brook opening and Branch River receiving join
correspondence.finding: The chosen northern opening is in the mapped Pike Brook corridor southwest of Long Mountain. The brook runs southeast through the Brookfield/Wakefield valley, receives the separately mapped Jack Brook and bends toward the Branch River west of Sanbornville. The selection follows that ordinary receiving corridor; its straightened positions do not reproduce every Pike Brook meander. Branch River is the next named receiving reach, rather than an alias of Pike Brook.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based original stored-part numbering within the selected fragment; component scopes can overlap at joins.

correspondence.component_scope: Branch River, Union Meadows and Union outlet
correspondence.finding: The named Branch River continues south beside the Route 16 corridor, through the broad mapped Union Meadows wetland/open-water setting, and into the Union/Branch River Reservoir setting. A mapped channel continues through Union and southeast beyond it. Lovell Lake is an eastern contributing/neighboring lake, not a lake traversed by this selection.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based original stored-part numbering within the selected fragment; component scopes can overlap at joins.

correspondence.component_scope: Branch River into the Salmon Falls pond system
correspondence.finding: Downstream of Union the Branch River follows the southeast valley past the Jones Brook entry and Laskey Corner, opening into the western arm of Northeast Pond. Salmon Falls River enters the same pond system from the north. The generalized selected approach shortcuts bends and the Branch River embayment but stays in the ordinary Branch-to-Northeast receiving setting; it is not interpreted as proof of a precise overland or artificial channel.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based original stored-part numbering within the selected fragment; component scopes can overlap at joins.

correspondence.component_scope: Northeast Pond, Milton Pond and their outlet
correspondence.finding: The route traverses Northeast Pond southward and continues through the connected narrowing and Milton Pond to the outlet at Milton. Town House Pond is a separately labeled connected western arm; no selected through-traverse of that whole arm is claimed. The Salmon Falls River label continues through the interpond and downstream receiving corridor. The map establishes ordinary lake/channel connections, without a claim about current levels or managed releases.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based original stored-part numbering within the selected fragment; component scopes can overlap at joins.

correspondence.component_scope: Salmon Falls River through Spaulding Pond and East Rochester
correspondence.finding: Below Milton the named Salmon Falls River passes through Spaulding Pond and follows the New Hampshire–Maine border corridor past North Rochester, then turns east through East Rochester/South Lebanon. Great Brook and Fall Brook are separately mapped side inflows; the Little River joins farther downstream. Each is distinguished from the selected main receiving route.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based original stored-part numbering within the selected fragment; component scopes can overlap at joins.

correspondence.component_scope: Berwick, Somersworth, Rollinsford and South Berwick
correspondence.finding: The selection continues along the repeatedly labeled Salmon Falls River through the widened and meandering corridor to Berwick/Somersworth, then through the Rollinsford/South Berwick reach. The river continues into a broad lower reach beside the Great Works River/Leighs Mill Pond joining setting. These urban and ponded reaches have a mapped onward connection; no current dam-operation assertion is made.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based original stored-part numbering within the selected fragment; component scopes can overlap at joins.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Salmon Falls join and Piscataqua estuary
correspondence.finding: The broad lower Salmon Falls corridor receives the Cocheco River from the west near the Dover/Rollinsford-side estuary and continues as the labeled Piscataqua River along Eliot. Sturgeon Creek is a distinct eastern tributary. Bellamy River and the Little Bay/Great Bay–Lamprey receiving complex are mapped west of the selected lower trunk; the selection continues down the Piscataqua rather than turning into those branches.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based original stored-part numbering within the selected fragment; component scopes can overlap at joins.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Piscataqua, Portsmouth Harbor and actual ending
correspondence.finding: The selected lower trunk follows the broad Piscataqua estuary past Bloody Point and South Eliot, the Portsmouth/Kittery crossings and the Seavey Island/Portsmouth Naval Shipyard island setting. The stored source ending is in the northern/western New Castle shoreline and Portsmouth Harbor setting; the rendered continuation ends farther south in the connected tidal-water/island-margin setting on the western side of New Castle near Leachs Island and Boatswain Hill. These are distinct endpoints. The generalized terminal segment shortcuts island/shoreline detail and is not asserted to be a straight, continuously wetted channel. The surrounding mapped harbor channels supply ordinary receiving-setting correspondence. Neither endpoint is silently moved to the outer Piscataqua mouth or the open Atlantic.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based original stored-part numbering within the selected fragment; component scopes can overlap at joins.

correspondence.component_scope: northwestern chosen opening and enclosed feeder
correspondence.finding: The selected opening is a small rocky/vegetated mountain hollow beside, rather than within, neighboring alpine lakes and snow patches. It turns south into a steep incised depression and then follows the continuous southeast wooded valley. The initial opening and descent are visibly part of the same terrain corridor; no lake-to-feeder transfer is required or asserted. No hydronym is assigned to this initial feeder.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based original stored-part numbering, restarting within each explicitly identified fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: upper valley to western lake head
correspondence.finding: The southeast valley continues into a visibly branching gravel/channel belt and fan at the northwestern lake head. The selected feeder-to-open-water transition is present in the inspected image, while nearby separate small lakes and neighboring valley entries are kept distinct.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based original stored-part numbering, restarting within each explicitly identified fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: great central lake passage
correspondence.finding: The selection traverses one continuous elongated lake, east through its bends and narrows to the developed eastern end. Its outline and adjoining independent southern lake distinguish the lake passage. NHC identifies this principal northern lake and its downstream relationship as Great Central Lake.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based original stored-part numbering, restarting within each explicitly identified fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: eastern lake outlet and northward stamp
correspondence.finding: At the eastern lake end the selected route turns north through the visible outlet/pond and channel corridor, then east into the larger receiving river. The ordinary lake-to-channel and receiving-junction connection is complete. NHC names the outlet river Stamp River, describes its junction with Ash River, and documents a controlled outlet; no current dam operation is inferred.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based original stored-part numbering, restarting within each explicitly identified fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: fragment join lower stamp and somass receiving corridor
correspondence.finding: The mainstem fragment boundary lies within the same continuously visible river corridor. The downstream selection follows southeast valley bends, open bars, agricultural margins and the western tributary confluence before the broad urban lower river. NHC distinguishes the Stamp reach from the Somass reach formed when Sproat River joins it. Exact name-transition vertices are not assigned.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based original stored-part numbering, restarting within each explicitly identified fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: actual source and render inlet endings
correspondence.finding: The last selected parts traverse the broad lower-river/estuarine floodplain to the head of the inlet beside the developed waterfront. The stored line generalizes the meander and tidal-margin setting rather than tracing the photographed bank. The source endpoint is at the eastern estuarine waterfront; the render endpoint is slightly farther south along the same connected inlet margin. Both endings are separately inspected and geographically continuous with the lower receiving water. NHC identifies the receiving inlet as Alberni Inlet.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based original stored-part numbering, restarting within each explicitly identified fragment.
